Based on the provided healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that common carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) can be used as an indicator of both cardiovascular phenotype and risk among adult black Africans. Our findings support CIMT as a significant indicator of both cardiovascular risk and phenotype among this population.

However, specific thresholds need to be defined based on prospective studies to determine the optimal ranges for identifying individuals with high cardiovascular risk or poor cardiovascular phenotype. It is essential to note that the surge in hypertension in Africa is largely explained by modifiable risk factors, such as lifestyle changes, which are crucial in preventing a catastrophic burden on the national health system.

While the available data suggest that CIMT can be used as an indicator of cardiovascular risk and phenotype among black Africans, further research is needed to confirm these findings and establish specific thresholds for defining individuals with high cardiovascular risk.
